info.title: MyLINK SMS API
info.description:
Purpose and functionality

MyLINK SMS API is a REST API supporting the needs for sending and receiving SMS to the recipients you want to reach, either if it is for time critical SMS or high load purposes.

MyLINK SMS API is LINK Mobility’s new flagship SMS product, and is a part of our CPaaS offering.

Current supported functionality

  • Send SMS (Mobile Terminated)
    • Send single message
    • Batch Sending MT Messages
  • Scheduling sendings
  • Receive SMS (Mobile Originated)
  • Delivery Reports
  • Message Obfuscation
  • Portal access for statistics and product administration

Getting started

  • Get in touch with us to get a demo or sign up for the product: Click here
  • Accept your invitation to the MyLINK portal to generate your API secrets
  • Revisit the developer portal for how to send an SMS

post.description:
The API allows you to batch up to a 1000 messages per request. When using batch sending you list all messages in an array. All parameters must be added per message in the batch sending.

Example
[
 	{
		"recipient": "+4712345678",
		"content": {
			"text": "Hello world",
			"options":{
				"sms.encoding":"AutoDetect",
				"sms.sender": "LINK",
				"sms.obfuscate": "ContentAndRecipient"
			}
		},
		"callback": {
			"mode": "URL",
			"urls": ["URL"]
		},
		"referenceId": "ref1"
	},
 	{
		"recipient": "+4787654321",
		"content": {
			"text": "Hello world 2",
			"options":{
				"sms.encoding":"AutoDetect",
				"sms.sender": "LINK",
				"sms.obfuscate": "ContentAndRecipient"
			}
		},
		"callback": {
			"mode": "URL",
			"urls": ["URL"]
		},
		"referenceId": "ref2"
	}
]

get.summary: Get a paginated list of scheduled messages

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: List of fields used to sort results

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Return schedule sending related with the same tag

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Return sending with scheduled date after start date

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Return sending with scheduled date before end date

code.description:
Status code
CodeNameDescriptionStatus Group
1AcceptedInitial status indicating message is accepted for processing. Accepted
2ScheduledInitial status indicating that a scheduled message is accepted for sending. Scheduled
1000QueuedMessage is currently queued in the SMSC (Short Message Service Centre) and will subsequently be forwarded to the operator. This is a regular process. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed yet). Queued
1001Sent to message gateway Message sent to message gateway. Sent
2000DeliveredMessage has been delivered to the final recipient. Delivered
3000Account validation errorUser, account or password could not be validated. Message was not sent. Rejected
3001Configuration errorAn error occurred in the provisioning of your account. Please contact Support for help. Message was not sent. Rejected
3002Invalid sender (source)The specified source (name or number) is invalid. Possible reasons: the sender you’re using is too long or you are using an unauthorized sender. Message was not sent. Rejected
3003Source type not supported Either short number, alpha or MSISDN are not allowed as sender (source) TON (type of number). Message was not sent. Rejected
3004Invalid recipientThe supplied recipient number is invalid. Possible reasons: the number is a landline number, the number is not assigned to an operator or the phone number is not formatted correctly. Message was not sent. Rejected
3005Destination type not supportedEither short number, alpha or MSISDN are not allowed as recipient (destination) TON (type of number). Message was not sent. Rejected
3006Encoding is not supportedOperator or country does not support the usage of GSM, UCS2 or binary encoding. Message was not sent. Rejected
3007Invalid message contentMessage content invalid or not supported by operator, device or country. Make sure that the message content is neither empty nor too long and that “TEXT” is used as data coding scheme (DCS). Message was not sent. Rejected
3008Invalid user data headerUser data headers are used to concatenate messages. User header might be formatted in a wrong way. Please contact Support for further assistance. Message was not sent. Rejected
3009Maximum throttling exceededThis may occur if too many messages are being sent per second to the SMSC (Short Message Service Centre) or the operator. Message was not sent. Rejected
3010ValidationOne or more validations Rejected
3011QuotaThis may occur if the quota for the messaging channel has been exceeded. Rejected
3013CountryBlockedThis may occur if the message is sent to a blocked country. Rejected
4000Generic errorUnexpected error. Message not delivered to the recipient. Contact Support for further assistance. Unable to send
4001Temporary routing errorThis may occur if your account is configured in a wrong way, our service is not ready to handle the message or the operator has reported a temporary error. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Unable to send
4002Permanent routing error This occurs if no route exists to the specified number. Contact Support for further assistance. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Unable to send
4003Phone number blockedThe recipient is permanently barred by the SMSC (Short Message Service Center) or operator. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Failed
4004Recipient temporarily barredRecipient barred. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Failed
4005Service provider errorError on operator side. Message has not been delivered. (In case of premium SMS: billing status unknown.) Failed
4006Operation blockedThe requested operation is not supported for the specified country, operator or recipient. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Failed
4007Not deliveredThe message has been sent to the operator but has not been delivered to the recipient. Please check if the phone number is formatted correctly. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed) Failed
4008ExpiredMessage has been sent to the operator but has not reached the recipient. It has been pending until the validity period (default 48h) has expired. Possible reasons: the phone is outside network coverage or turned off. (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Failed
4009TimeoutThis may occur if a message is being processed, but the response is taking too long time to wait. Final status unknown. (In case of premium SMS: billing status unknown.) Failed
4010Delivery report is not supportedOperator does not support the usage of delivery reports. Failed
4011Deleted by operatorMessage has been deleted at the operator side in the SMSC (Short Message Service Centre). (In case of premium SMS: message not billed.) Failed
5000Retried to send message to Gateway and will retry sending again Retried

urls.description: List of URLs to receive DLRs on. Mandatory when using mode "URL" - not relevant to any other modes.

gateId.description: The ID of the callback to be used. Can be set up in the Callbacks section of MyLINK portal. Mandatory when using mode "Gate" - not relevant to any other modes.

MessageCallbackMode.description: Choose how you want to receive your Delivery reports. Mode Profile sends any DLRs towards your default configuration in MyLINK portal), URL sends towards a list of urls provided in the request, Gate sends towards a referenced configuration from MyLINK portal, or None (no DLR is sent anywhere). Each mode requires different request parameters, refer to the fields below.

relative.description: Time specified in milliseconds of how long the message is supposed to live. The maximum value is 48 hours (172800000 milliseconds), which is also the default.

absolute.description: Absolute time specified of when this message should expire. ISO8601 formatted string in UTC.

MessagePriority.description: Set priority on your own messages. Priority only affects your own queue.

relative.description: Time specified in milliseconds of how much we will offset the message in the future. The maximum value is 3 months (7_889_232_000 milliseconds), which is also the default. The minimum value is 600000 ms (10 minutes)

absolute.description: Absolute time specified of when this message should be sent. ISO8601 formatted string in UTC.

tag.description: A tag for the message schedule. Can be used to group schedules by tag

channel.description: Channel used for sending: SMS, whatsApp, rcs, email

timestamp.description: Timestamp when event occurred in provider infrastructure

routeId.description: Identifier of route used for matching message

routeKeyword.description: Keyword of route used for matching message

url.description: Location url i.e. google maps or similar.

timeOffset.description: Offset set from UTC in milliseconds

type.description: Status type: accepted, queued, sent, retried, rejected, delivered, failed, read, typing

text.description: A single message can be 160 characters (GSM encoding). If message exceeds 160 characters each message part will be split in to 153 characters. Maximum length of a message is dependent on the operator you are sending towards.UCS2 encoding: 70/67 characters single/multipart.

requestId.description: Unique Id of the request made towards LINK

SmsMessageObfuscateOptions.description: Obfuscation allows you to anonymize content and recipient or content only after the message is processed. Non-retrievable.

sms.sender.description: SenderID of the message. Can be numeric or alphanumeric. Restrictions may apply in different countries.

recipient.description: Recipients must be provided in MSISDN format. Remember that MSISDN must have a leading (+). Example: +4712345678

referenceId.description: Your own internal transaction ID. Not used for anything except as a reference. Optional.

requestId.description: Unique Id of the request made towards LINK

post.description:
Getting started

Mobile originated message content

Mobile originated (MO) SMS can be used to interact with the end-user, and can be done in several ways.

First of all, you need access to a type of number to receive MO’s on your product. Currently, you can use

  • Short code
    • User friendly format, easy to remember. Excellent for branding.
    • It is possible to have access to a short code, either as shared (with other clients) or dedicated (you own the usage exclusively)
    • Country specific number to receive SMS to your endpoint. Use of short code is limited to the country it is issued in. Example: Only end users with a Swedish MSISDN can send to a Swedish short code
  • Long number
    • Long number is a number in MSISDN format used for receiving messages.
    • The long number from each country reflects the actual number length relevant for the country it is issued in.
    • Long number may be used internationally (dependent on operator support)
  • Subnumber
    • Certain short codes can be extended with subnumbers. Subnumbers are extra digits added to the end of the original access number.
    • Typical usage of subnumbers is to create dialogue-based SMS applications, where the end user does not need to use a specific SMS keyword when replying to a message.
    • Subnumbering is currently only supported in Finland and Norway

Keyword

  • Keyword is often used to determine a specific service. It is used both on shared and dedicated numbers.
  • A keyword can be set up using different matching rules:
    • Exact. Incoming message must contain exactly the keyword string defined
    • Starts with. Incoming message must begin with the keyword defined
    • First word. Incoming message contains the first word of the keyword defined
